latest.scope: Fixed training-val subset; synthetic interventions with identical noisy history. Correct-current uses oracle current target and quality=1 as a diagnostic, not deployable extra GT or proof of physics.

best.scope: Fixed training-val subset; synthetic interventions with identical noisy history. Correct-current uses oracle current target and quality=1 as a diagnostic, not deployable extra GT or proof of physics.

summary.interpretation: Temporal restoration improves over last-history hold, but these input controls indicate dominant reliance on history and inadequate preservation of accurate current observations when the history is noisy. This is not proof of zero current-input dependence.
summary.cause_hypothesis: Training code gives histories 4mm/1.5deg noise vs current 25mm/12deg/8deg, clean cases remove both noises together, and quality hints are not calibrated to actual errors. These settings may favor the history; no corrective retraining was performed.

coverage.aggregation: Within-source sample mean, then equal mean of four sources; percent and quantile macro averages are not pooled proportions/quantiles.

artifacts.initial_launch_failure: First controller mkdir lacked parents=True; failed before snapshots or inference; repaired directory creation and launched once.

limits: Synthetic corruption and GT-based histories, not real HaWoR estimates or own-history closed-loop rollout.
Fitted MANO reference wrist/rotations, not independent raw-sensor accuracy or joint/mesh reconstruction.
Full validation overlaps and is used for tuning; no independent test claim or confidence interval.
Correct-current/noisy-history is a deliberately privileged diagnostic intervention, not inference using unavailable GT.
Earlier best has slightly lower selection loss, while latest has lower mean finger and clean errors; no universal winner or deployment approval.
